stage1.impression: It's a warm, hazy night bar with a convincing depth of stools, pendants and a record wall, but it reads as a competent CG render rather than a photograph. Everything is the same orange-brown timber, so the concrete and steel shell isn't there. The pendants and the right-hand speaker niche glow milky white and blown, the half-empty record cubbies glow brighter than anything else, and the hero speakers read as grey boxes behind a reflection rather than tinted cast acrylic. As it stands a magazine would see a generic brown hotel bar, not a specific place, even though the speakers-in-niches idea is specific.

blocking_9: The hero speaker in the left niche must read at a glance as smoked cast acrylic: glowing polished edges, the batts visible through a tint, no blown horn mouth (niche region clip_pct < 0.3, lum_median 60-110)
The Dome pendants must read as smoked acrylic with a frosted liner, not opal white glass (dome lum_median < 170, clip_pct < 0.5)
The record wall must be full of records and must not be the brightest thing in the frame (lum_median <= 100)

The board-formed concrete, Douglas fir and blackened steel shell must be legible as different materials under a less orange grade (frame b_median >= 32 and the ceiling no longer a flat orange monotone)
The foreground chair silhouette must hold some detail (lum_median >= 12) or be moved out of the frame
Some sign of life must be readable at a glance near the speaker niche (the record out of its sleeve, the coat), not lost in the tiny glassware
To be published as a specific place rather than a generic bar, the speakers-in-niches and the zinc counter must carry the frame, and the record wall's peach glow must stop competing with them

defects.what: Dome pendant reads as opal white glass; lum_median 224, clip 0.85 %; no smoked tint visible (delta-E2000 62 against a smoked #3A3532)
The second Dome is blown out: clip 4.4 %
Right speaker niche washed out: lum_median 148, clip 0.95 %; the speaker reads as a pale grey box and the horn mouth/top is near white
Left speaker's horn mouth shows a flat white plane (p95 242) that reads like a reflection card, not resin
Left hero speaker reads grey and metallic behind a reflective plane; no glowing acrylic edges, no tint read; the niche's top LED strip is a hard white line
Record wall cubbies are mostly empty and glow peach; at median 130 they are the brightest large area of the frame and read as unfinished shelving
Foreground tub chair is a crushed black slab: lum_median 4.5, crush 10.9 %
Ceiling beams are a flat orange monotone (lum_range 39, b_median 11) with no checks, nail holes or end grain; reads as a textured CG plane
Global grade too orange/sepia: r 70 / g 42 / b 24 median; concrete, oak, fir and steel all collapse into one brown
Clear acrylic on the counter (the record player's posts and lid) reads as a thin display case or vitrine, with thin glossy edges
A diagonal light shaft through the haze looks like a stage beam with no visible source
Row of identical stools and counter chairs, repeated copies of one model; the floor at the right reads as blotchy stone with denoiser smear
The far speaker reads as a small grey box hung on the wall, unrelated to the hero's look

changes.problem: The lit niches flood the speakers, so the hero reads as a washed grey box with a blown horn instead of tinted acrylic.

evidence.measured: lum_median 148, p95 248, clip 0.95 %; left niche horn p95 242

changes.expected: The niches become a soft glow behind the speakers; the cabinet edges and the white batts read through the smoked tint; no clipping in the niche.

changes.problem: The Dome pendants read as opal white glass, not smoked acrylic with a frosted liner, and two of them clip.

evidence.measured: lum_median 224, clip 0.85 %; second Dome [645,270,698,305] clip 4.4 %; delta-E2000 62 vs #3A3532

changes.expected: The shade shows its smoked outer skin with a warm, lower glow from the liner and a bright rim only at the lower lip; light still lands on the zinc from the downlights.

changes.problem: The record wall is mostly empty glowing cubbies, the brightest large area of the frame, and it reads as unfinished shelving that pulls the eye from the speakers.

evidence.measured: lum_median 130, r_median 169; the frame's median is 47

change.setting: props: records on the record wall, plus the record wall spots
change.from: cubbies largely empty; 4 x spot 12.0 W
change.to: every cubby filled with spines (some leaning, a few face-out sleeves); 4 x spot 6.0 W

changes.expected: A dense dark wall of spines with small highlights, sitting about a stop below the speaker niches.

changes.problem: The grade is so orange that concrete, oak, fir and steel collapse into one brown and the shell isn't legible.

evidence.measured: medians r 70 / g 42 / b 24; ceiling b_median 11

changes.expected: The practicals still read warm, but the concrete turns a warm grey and the steel near black; the timber separates from the concrete.

changes.problem: The foreground tub chair is a crushed black slab that takes the bottom-left of the frame without describing leather or form.

change.setting: candles (point lamps) and the sink's under-glow
change.to: candles 2 x 6.0 W, with one votive moved to the counter edge nearest the camera; sink under-glow 1.2

changes.problem: The ceiling beams and the walls read as a uniform CG timber texture, and the fir's checks, nail holes and end grain aren't there.

evidence.measured: lum_range 39, p5 21.5 / p95 60.7: a flat field

changes.problem: A diagonal haze shaft at the right reads as a theatrical stage beam with no visible source.

changes.expected: The air keeps a little atmosphere around the pendants, without hard shafts.

changes.problem: The foreground chair and the stool row take the lower third, while the hero speaker sits small at the far left behind the bar's reflection.

evidence.measured: the hero speaker takes about 5 % of the frame; lum_median 69 against a 47 frame

change.to: position [3.6, 3.0, 1.25], 40 mm, looking at [7.2, 5.6, 1.35], focus on the left niche speaker

out_of_scope.request: Make the clear acrylic on the counter (the record player's posts and base) thicker, with polished glowing edges, so it doesn't read as a display case
out_of_scope.why: EARF's products (R3 Float) are fixed in shape and parts

out_of_scope.request: Give the speakers in the niches more visible tint and edge glow through the material itself
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's colour and parts are fixed; only the lighting (c1) may change

out_of_scope.request: Vary the stool and counter-chair models so they don't look like copies
out_of_scope.why: The seats are fixed in the room's design

out_of_scope.request: Show more of the board-formed concrete shell in place of the timber lining
out_of_scope.why: The room's materials and layout are fixed
